- Default hosted behavior: Redwood’s hosted API collects telemetry and artifacts used for diagnostics and quality. Request/response artifacts (prompts + full model outputs) are retained by default for a defined window; retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private.
- Residency: Hosted customers are served in region-specific clusters; you can request US-only residency for your org, but strict residency + short retention windows (30 days) are most straightforward on Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Immediate purge: We support account-level purge requests; Neha will spell out the purge workflow, time-to-complete, and confirmation artifact you can reference in the SOW.

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear questions. Below is an operational summary you can include in the SOW and a short description of the purge runbook. I attached the full runbook for your legal/security review.

Summary (concise):
- Classification: We treat prompts (the request payload you send) and outputs (model generations) as customer data. Both are considered "artifacts" for the purpose of retention and eDiscovery.
- Default retention (hosted API): By default, hosted accounts retain request/response artifacts for 60 days. This retention is used for debugging, quality monitoring, and abuse detection; access is limited to authorized SRE/security staff and is audited.
- Telemetry vs artifacts: Aggregated telemetry (latency/error metrics, token-level usage aggregates) is retained separately for 24 months for platform analytics; these aggregates do not contain raw prompt/output text.
- Residency: We operate region-specific clusters. Hosted US-only residency is available — we route your account to US clusters and flag data boundaries. However, hosted mode with a 30-day hard purge is operationally possible but carries tradeoffs (reduced time for quality regressions/detection). For strict contractual guarantees around residency + short retention windows, Redwood Dedicated or Private is recommended.

Purge runbook (summary; see attached full runbook):
1) Customer files a purge request via support portal + DPA clause reference.
2) We schedule the purge job scoped to the account and artifact classes (prompts, outputs, cached prefixes).
3) Backend sequenced steps: zero traffic writes; mark data for deletion; issue storage-level deletion (S3 lifecycle + secure wipe for ephemeral caches); update search/index manifests; rotate any derived ephemeral caches.
4) Cryptographic confirmation: if keys were customer-managed (KMS), we will provide key rotation/expiry records.
5) Confirmation: Customer receives a purge confirmation document and deletion job ID. Typical completion: hosted accounts 24–72 hours depending on data volume; Dedicated/Private — timing determined by contract and on-prem scheduling.

Operational notes:
- Legal holds: If a legal hold is in place, purges are paused until lifted.
- Backups: Backups are retained per backup retention policy; purge runbook includes steps to scrub backups to the extent permitted by the backup medium and backup window — we include backup purge/retention language in the SOW when needed.
- Access: Red team/internal audit access is strictly logged and requires approved ticketing.

I’ve attached the detailed runbook and the retention matrix with explicit artifact classes and timelines. Happy to jump on a short call with your security team to walk through any items you want to tighten in the contract language.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
